name: The Cypriot harbor
intro:
The harbor is smaller than Ugarit's and busier in a different way. Nobody is writing anything down.

Copper sits in the yard in stacks, dull where it has cooled. A woman splits ingots with a wedge and a boy carries the pieces. The houses are stone at the base and mud above, roofs of reed and earth, and the light off the white walls is a physical thing you have to turn away from.

People speak to each other in a tongue you cannot follow. They speak to you in Akkadian, slowly, and then in gestures, and then — a clay tablet held up, a mark traced with a thumb — in a kind of writing that is not cuneiform and that nobody here will read aloud for you.

The wind is steady. Everything smells of the workshop and the sea at once.

places.name: The copper yard
places.description: Ingots by weight, and a broker who will tell you what they are worth elsewhere before you ask.

places.name: The landing
places.description: Boats drawn up on the shingle, nets mended in the shade, and a passage back to the mainland to arrange.

places.name: The smithy
places.description: A workshop open on one side to the yard, where a girl of nine sorts charcoal by size while her mother works the bronze.

places.name: The inn
places.description: Two rooms and a courtyard where travelers are fed and quietly assessed.

night.text: The yard is quiet. A kiln still glows at the edge of the town, frogs keep at the cistern, and the sea is louder at night than it has any right to be.

stateNotes.busy: The yard is working at full tilt; everyone here has somewhere else to be.

sources: Late Cypriot copper production and harbor settlements, general
provenance.notes: Copper working and maritime exchange are well attested. The settlement, its people, and its prices are a composite invented for play.
